title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: JFrog
providers.scope_notes: Covers JFrog Platform (Cloud/SaaS). JFrog Cloud SaaS; IP allowlist, OIDC integration and MyJFrog API tokens need Enterprise X or Enterprise+, log streaming needs Enterprise+, Cloud Log Collection is on all SaaS licenses; several token thresholds are documented only as self-hosted YAML settings.

controls.name: Revoke Token by ID / Access Tokens page
controls.what: Admin revokes any token; users revoke their own.
controls.setting: Administration > User Management > Access Tokens; DELETE /access/api/v1/tokens/{tokenId}

controls.name: Revoke Token by Value
controls.what: Admin revokes a leaked JWT or reference token by its value.

controls.name: Token default expiry
controls.what: Sets the default expiry for new tokens.

controls.name: token.max-expiry
controls.what: Caps non-admin token lifetime and blocks non-expiring tokens when set above 0.

controls.name: IP/CIDR Allowlist
controls.what: Only listed IPs/JPDs can reach the JPD.
controls.setting: MyJFrog > Security > Allowlist; MyJFrog IP allowlist API

controls.name: Disable/delete user (with SCIM)
controls.what: Deleting or disabling a user revokes their identity tokens; SCIM pushes IdP deprovisioning.

no_control.what: Tokens with expiry shorter than the revocable threshold (default 6 hours) cannot be revoked.

controls_unknown: Whether SaaS customers can change token.max-expiry, token.allow-refreshable or revocable-expiry-threshold (documented only as Access YAML settings).
A setting to stop non-admin users creating identity tokens.
Default and maximum lifetime of UI-generated identity tokens.
Whether the IP allowlist covers the MyJFrog portal API.
Whether MyJFrog audit logs record API token generation (event names not listed).
Reference token length: Access Tokens page says 128 characters, Identity Tokens page says 64.

auth_paths.name: Access tokens (scoped tokens: admin, user, group and project scopes; reference token form)

authentication.summary: JWT issued by JFrog Access, sent as Bearer; a 'reference token' alias can be used as a password for basic auth. Admins can mint tokens for any subject, including non-existent (transient) users and CI jobs. Tokens can also authenticate on other JPDs in the same circle of trust.

federation.details: Tokens are independent of the IdP session. Without SCIM, a user removed from the IdP can keep refreshing tokens.

ip_restriction.boundary: MyJFrog IP/CIDR allowlist blocks all traffic to the JPD from non-listed IPs (Enterprise X/Enterprise+). Off by default.

lifetime.summary: Default 1h; expiry 0 = never expires unless admin sets a max expiry

renewal.expiry_basis: refreshable tokens can be refreshed by the holder
renewal.summary: Optional refresh token; otherwise create a new token.

administration.summary: Admins see and revoke all tokens (UI User Management > Access Tokens, or REST). Project admins can mint project tokens. Tokens shorter than the revocable threshold (default 6h) cannot be revoked.
administration.conditions: Max expiry, refreshable and revocable thresholds are documented as Access YAML settings; SaaS customer control not documented.

sso.details: Tokens are not re-checked against the IdP; a user disabled in the IdP may still refresh tokens unless SCIM pushes the change.

offboard.details: SCIM deprovisioning disables the user and blocks refreshes; JFrog says to revoke active tokens explicitly for immediate termination.

inventory.details: Administration > User Management > Access Tokens page and GET /access/api/v1/tokens (admins see all).

usage.ui: Administration > Artifactory > System Logs (access log; auth type field = TOKEN, filter by username). SaaS: download Audit Trail and Request logs from the jfrog-logs repository

reads.ui: Request log (jfrog-logs repo on SaaS): filter Request method=POST and Request URL containing api/search/aql, plus Username

kill.ui: Administration > User Management > Access Tokens > select token > Revoke

offboard.ui: Administration > User Management > Users (disable/delete user), then revoke the user's tokens under User Management > Access Tokens

token_format.notes: Reference tokens start with cmVmd; full tokens are JWTs (eyJ...).

log_sources.name: Audit Trail Log (access-security-audit)
log_sources.notes: Token create/update/delete; via Cloud Log Collection (all SaaS licenses, jfrog-logs repo, up to 24h delay) or Log Streaming (Enterprise+).

log_sources.name: Artifactory Request Log
log_sources.notes: Every HTTP request with username and remote address.

log_sources.name: Artifactory Access Log
log_sources.notes: Logins, deploys with auth type APIKEY or TOKEN; SaaS omits DOWNLOAD events by default.

credential_id_fields.notes: Token entity; exact ID content not documented.

lifecycle_events.notes: Event Type C on entity TKN.
Event Type D on entity TKN.

anomaly_cues: Tokens with no expiry or for transient subjects
Admin-scoped tokens created outside change windows
Large AQL queries or mass downloads in the request log

containment.steps: Revoke by ID or by value; disable the user; for refreshable tokens without SCIM, disable the JFrog user directly.
containment.notes: Tokens below the revocable threshold (default 6h) cannot be revoked and run to expiry.

unknown: Exact token identifier in audit trail entries

calls.log_notes: Request log records all HTTP requests.
Request log; body not logged per documented fields.
